downgraded.text: Is a dragon: Karadžić refers the ala to the aždaha, which he glosses as a dragon (Latin draco).
downgraded.to_text: Karadžić refers the ala to the aždaha, which he glosses as a dragon (Latin draco).
downgraded.reason: The lead "Is a dragon:" asserts identity; the Ала f. entry gives only a "vide аждаха" cross-reference and in the same sentence sets the ala apart from the aždaha by its particular spiritual power. Cut to the cross-reference and the gloss the pages print.

flagged.text: It is thought that the ala has a particular spiritual power beyond that of the aždaha.
flagged.reason: Translation choice: "да алу се мисли да има од аждахе особиту духовну силу" can be read "beyond/more than the aždaha" or "apart from (distinct from) the aždaha"; Afanasyev p.519 quotes the sentence without "од аждахе", so it does not settle the reading.

grade_rationale.text: Every surviving clause rests on Karadžić’s dictionary entry for the ala (Ала f., "види аждаха"), one 19th-century collector.
Afanasyev’s account of the ala quotes Karadžić’s dictionary (his footnote 5, "Срп. речник"), so it is not independent of Karadžić and is counted once with him.
The only people named for the ala is the Serbs ("Въ Сербіи"); no other source in the corpus records it.
